🎨 前端 / Frontend — Day 26: Prototypes & `this` — How JS Objects Really Work

> 阶段 / Phase: Mastery | 类别 / Category: JavaScript Core | Week 6 | 阅读时间 / Read time: ~2 min

真实场景 / Real Scenario

你在 code review 中看到同事写了这段代码：


class Button {
  constructor(label) {
    this.label = label;
  }
  click() {
    console.log(`Clicked: ${this.label}`);
  }
}

const btn = new Button("Submit");
document.getElementById("btn").addEventListener("click", btn.click);
// User clicks → what happens?

点击后输出什么？

🤔 猜猜看 / Pop Quiz

点击按钮后，控制台输出是？/ What does the console log?

A) "Clicked: Submit"

B) "Clicked: undefined"

C) TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined

D) Nothing, no error

<details><summary>显示答案 / Show Answer</summary>

答案：B — "Clicked: undefined"

原因：btn.click 作为回调传入时，this 绑定丢失了。事件触发时 this 指向 DOM 元素（<button>），而不是 btn 实例，所以 this.label 是 undefined。

Reason: When btn.click is passed as a callback, the this binding is lost. When the event fires, this refers to the DOM element, not the btn instance.

</details>

原型链 / Prototype Chain

JavaScript 中，每个对象都有一个隐式指针指向它的"原型"。当你访问一个属性，JS 先在对象本身找，找不到就沿着原型链往上找。


const btn = new Button("Submit");

// btn 的原型链：
// btn → Button.prototype → Object.prototype → null

// 查找 btn.click 的过程：
// 1. btn 自身有 click 属性吗？❌
// 2. Button.prototype 有吗？✅ → 找到了


// 可以直接验证：
console.log(btn.__proto__ === Button.prototype); // true
console.log(Button.prototype.__proto__ === Object.prototype); // true

// class 语法是 prototype 的语法糖：
// class Button {} === function Button() {} + Button.prototype.click = ...

`this` 绑定规则 / The 4 Rules of `this`


// 规则 1: 默认绑定 — 独立调用时 this = global/undefined(strict)
function greet() { console.log(this); }
greet(); // window (browser) or undefined (strict mode)

// 规则 2: 隐式绑定 — 方法调用时 this = 调用它的对象
const obj = { name: "Alice", greet() { console.log(this.name); } };
obj.greet(); // "Alice" ✅

// 规则 3: 显式绑定 — call/apply/bind
greet.call({ name: "Bob" }); // "Bob"
const boundGreet = obj.greet.bind({ name: "Charlie" });
boundGreet(); // "Charlie"

// 规则 4: new 绑定 — 构造函数中 this = 新创建的对象
const btn = new Button("Submit"); // this = btn

❌ 常见错误 vs ✅ 正确做法


// ❌ 错误：this 绑定丢失
document.getElementById("btn").addEventListener("click", btn.click);
// 点击时 this = DOM element，不是 btn

// ✅ 方法 1：bind
document.getElementById("btn").addEventListener("click", btn.click.bind(btn));

// ✅ 方法 2：箭头函数（推荐，更简洁）
document.getElementById("btn").addEventListener("click", () => btn.click());
// 箭头函数没有自己的 this，捕获外层 this

// ✅ 方法 3：类字段语法（React 中最常见）
class Button {
  label: string;
  // 箭头函数作为类字段 — this 永远绑定到实例
  click = () => {
    console.log(`Clicked: ${this.label}`);
  };
}
// 代价：每个实例都有一份 click 函数的拷贝（vs 原型方法共享一份）

箭头函数 vs 普通函数的 this / Arrow vs Regular


class Timer {
  constructor() {
    this.seconds = 0;
  }
  
  // ❌ 普通函数：this 丢失
  startWrong() {
    setInterval(function() {
      this.seconds++; // this = window/undefined!
    }, 1000);
  }
  
  // ✅ 箭头函数：捕获外层 this
  startCorrect() {
    setInterval(() => {
      this.seconds++; // this = Timer instance ✅
    }, 1000);
  }
}

核心规则：箭头函数没有自己的 this，它"继承"外层作用域的 this。

Arrow functions don't have their own this — they inherit it from the enclosing lexical scope.

何时用 / When to Use

| 场景 | 选择 |

|------|------|

| React class 组件方法 | 类字段箭头函数 handleClick = () => {} |

| 原型方法（共享逻辑）| 普通方法 method() {} |

| 回调中需要 this | 箭头函数 () => this.xxx |

| 工具库 polyfill | .bind(context) |

| 需要动态 this | 普通函数 + 显式绑定 |

📚 References

1. [MDN — this keyword](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/this)

2. [MDN — Inheritance and the prototype chain](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Inheritance_and_the_prototype_chain)

3. [You Don't Know JS — this & Object Prototypes](https://github.com/getify/You-Dont-Know-JS/tree/2nd-ed/objects-classes)

🧒 ELI5 / 小孩版解释

JavaScript 里的 this 就像"代词我"——它的意思取决于说话的人是谁。如果你把"我的名字"这句话录下来，播放给别人，"我"就会变成播放的人，而不是你。bind() 就像把"我"直接替换成你的名字，这样不管谁播放都是对的。原型链就像家族遗传——找不到的属性就去问"父辈"。

In JS, this is like the word "I" — it depends on WHO is speaking. If you record "my name is..." and play it for someone else, "my" becomes them, not you. bind() is like replacing "my" with your actual name so it's always correct. Prototype chains are like family genes — if you don't have a trait, check your parents.

Review

🔄 复习日 / Review Day — Day 30 (2026-04-23)

📊 NeetCode: 26/150 · SysDesign: 25/40 · Behavioral: 25/40 · Frontend: 25/50 · AI: 12/30

🔥 2-day streak!

🔄 复习日 / Review Day

今天是复习日！回顾过去4天的内容。

It's review day! Let's consolidate the last 4 days of learning.

覆盖的主题 / Topics Covered:

- Day 26: Autocomplete/Typeahead · Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation · Handling Tough Feedback · TypeScript Generics · AI Agents (ReAct)

- Day 28: Chat System Design · Daily Temperatures · Build-vs-Buy · Promises & async/await · MCP Protocol

- Day 29: Search Engine Design · Car Fleet · Navigating Org Change · Event Loop · AI News

📝 Quick Quiz — 3 Mini-Reviews

Q1: [🏗️ System Design] 你在设计一个类似 Slack 的聊天系统时，为什么要用 WebSocket 而不是 HTTP 轮询？能说出至少两个技术理由吗？

When designing a chat system like Slack/WhatsApp, why prefer WebSockets over HTTP polling? Name at least two technical reasons.

<details><summary>显示答案 / Show Answer</summary>

WebSocket 的核心优势在于双向持久连接。HTTP 轮询需要客户端反复发起请求（每次都有 TCP 握手和 HTTP 头开销），而 WebSocket 建立一次连接后双方可随时推送数据。

具体理由：

1. 低延迟：WebSocket 消息延迟通常 <100ms；轮询间隔造成人为延迟（1-30s）

2. 更低开销：WebSocket 帧头只有 2-10 字节，HTTP 请求头动辄几百字节

3. 服务端推送：服务器可主动推送新消息，无需客户端反复问"有新消息吗？"

4. 连接效率：避免了海量用户同时轮询造成的"惊群效应"

Key insight: WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection established via HTTP Upgrade. Once connected, either side can send data at any time — perfect for real-time chat where the server needs to push messages to clients without them asking.

</details>

Q2: [💻 Algorithms] 在 "Car Fleet" 问题中，为什么要先按起始位置从大到小排序？如果不排序直接用栈会出现什么问题？

In the Car Fleet problem, why must you sort cars by starting position in descending order before using the stack? What goes wrong without sorting?

<details><summary>显示答案 / Show Answer</summary>

核心洞察： 车队的形成依赖于"追及关系"——只有后车能追上前车才能合并成车队。按位置从大到小排序，相当于从最靠近终点的车开始处理，确保每辆车的"追及对象"已经确定。

如果不排序，你无法知道一辆车的"前方是谁"——会错误地把不相邻的车配对，导致错误的车队合并计算。

算法流程：


sort cars by position descending (closest to target first)
for each car:
    time_to_arrive = (target - position) / speed
    if stack is empty OR time > stack[-1]:
        stack.append(time)   # new fleet
    # else: this car catches up → same fleet, discard
return len(stack)

直觉： 如果一辆车计算出的到达时间 ≤ 前方最近车队的到达时间，说明它会在到达前被"挡住"，合并入同一车队。栈顶永远是当前最近的车队时间。

</details>

Q3: [🎨 Frontend] 下面这段代码有什么问题？Event Loop 中 Promise.resolve() 和 setTimeout(() => {}, 0) 谁先执行？


console.log('1');
setTimeout(() => console.log('2'), 0);
Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log('3'));
console.log('4');

What will the output order be, and why?

<details><summary>显示答案 / Show Answer</summary>

输出顺序： 1 → 4 → 3 → 2

原因： JavaScript 事件循环有两种任务队列：

| 队列类型 | 英文 | 例子 | 优先级 |

|---------|------|------|--------|

| 微任务 | Microtask Queue | Promise.then, queueMicrotask, MutationObserver | 高 |

| 宏任务 | Macrotask Queue | setTimeout, setInterval, I/O | 低 |

执行顺序：

1. 同步代码先执行：console.log('1') → console.log('4')（同步，顺序执行）

2. setTimeout 回调进入宏任务队列

3. Promise.then 回调进入微任务队列

4. 当前调用栈清空后，先清空所有微任务：console.log('3')

5. 最后处理宏任务：console.log('2')

关键规则： 每次宏任务执行完毕后，会把当前微任务队列全部清空，然后才执行下一个宏任务。Promise.resolve() 虽然是异步，但属于微任务，比 setTimeout(0) 更早执行。

</details>

💡 复习巩固记忆，螺旋式上升。每一次回顾都让知识更牢固。

Review strengthens memory. Each revisit makes knowledge more durable.

📅 明天继续新内容！Tomorrow: fresh content continues.

item.description:
🏗️ System Design

🏗️ 系统设计 / System Design — Design a Search Engine

场景 / Scenario:

想象你在设计 Google 或 Bing 的核心搜索功能。用户输入查询，你需要在几毫秒内从数十亿个网页中返回最相关的结果。

Imagine you are designing the core search functionality of Google or Bing. A user enters a query, and you need to return the most relevant results from billions of web pages in milliseconds.

架构图 / Architecture Diagram:


[User] --> [Load Balancer] --> [Web Servers]
                                     |
                                     v
                            [Query Processor]
                               /           \
                              /             \
                    [Index Cluster]    [Document Store]
                    (Inverted Index)   (HTML/Snippets)
                             |
                      [Ranker / ML]

核心权衡 / Key Tradeoffs:

1. Inverted Index (倒排索引): 为什么不直接搜网页？因为太慢。倒排索引将单词映射到包含该单词的文档列表（就像书后的索引），极大加快了查询速度。/ Why not just search web pages directly? Too slow. An inverted index maps words to a list of documents containing them (like an index at the back of a book), drastically speeding up queries.

2. Crawling vs Indexing (爬取 vs 索引): 爬虫（Crawler）异步抓取网页，索引器（Indexer）离线构建索引。查询时只访问索引，不接触爬虫。/ Crawlers fetch pages asynchronously, and Indexers build the index offline. Queries only hit the index, never the crawlers.

3. Ranking (排名): 仅找到文档不够，还需要根据相关性（如 PageRank、TF-IDF、机器学习模型）进行排序。/ Finding documents isn't enough; they must be sorted by relevance (e.g., PageRank, TF-IDF, ML models).

常见误区 / Common Mistakes:

- ❌ 实时更新索引 (Real-time index updates): 每次有新网页就更新整个索引。/ Updating the entire index every time a new page is found.

- ✅ 正确做法 (Correct approach): 使用主索引（只读，定期构建）和辅助/内存索引（处理新文档），查询时合并结果。/ Use a main index (read-only, built periodically) and an auxiliary/in-memory index (for new docs), merging results at query time.

📚 参考文献 / References:

- [Elasticsearch Architecture](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/elasticsearch-intro.html)

- [How Google Search Works](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/)

- [System Design: Search Engine](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/design-a-search-engine-system-design-interview/)

🧒 ELI5 (Explain Like I'm 5):

搜索引擎就像一个超级图书管理员。他不一页一页翻书找答案，而是提前做了一个巨大的“词汇表”，记录了每个词在哪些书的哪一页。你一问，他查词汇表，瞬间就把书找出来了！

A search engine is like a super librarian. Instead of flipping through books page by page to find answers, they made a giant "vocabulary list" beforehand, recording which books and pages contain each word. When you ask, they check the list and find the books instantly!

💻 Algorithms

💻 算法 / Algorithms — #853 Car Fleet (Medium) — Stack

🧩 单调栈模式 (6/7) — building on the template from Day X

场景 / Real-world analogy:

想象你在高速公路上开车，前面有一辆慢车。你不能超车，只能减速跟在它后面，你们就成了一个“车队”。有多少个这样的车队能到达终点？

Imagine driving on a highway behind a slow car. You can't pass it, so you slow down and follow it, forming a "fleet." How many such fleets will reach the destination?

问题 / Problem:

有 n 辆车在单车道上行驶，目标是 target。每辆车有初始位置 position[i] 和速度 speed[i]。如果一辆车追上前面的车，它必须降速并与前车组成一个车队（视为一个整体）。求到达终点时的车队数量。

There are n cars driving on a single-lane road to a target. Each car has an initial position[i] and speed[i]. If a car catches up to the one ahead, it must slow down and form a fleet (treated as one entity). Find the number of car fleets arriving at the target.

映射到模板 / Map to pattern template:

- 排序 (Sort): 首先按位置降序排序（离终点近的在前面）。/ Sort by position descending (closest to target first).

- 时间 (Time): 计算每辆车到达终点所需的时间 (target - pos) / speed。/ Calculate time to reach target for each car.

- 单调栈 (Monotonic Stack): 维护到达时间。如果后面的车（栈顶）比前面的车（栈顶的下一个）时间短或等于，说明它能追上，形成车队（弹出后面的车）。/ Maintain arrival times. If a car behind (top of stack) takes less or equal time than the car ahead (next in stack), it catches up, forming a fleet (pop the car behind).

Python 代码 / Python Solution:


def carFleet(target: int, position: List[int], speed: List[int]) -> int:
    # 1. 组合并按位置降序排序 / Combine and sort by position descending
    cars = sorted(zip(position, speed), reverse=True)
    stack = []
    
    # 2. 遍历每辆车 / Iterate through each car
    for pos, spd in cars:
        # 计算到达时间 / Calculate arrival time
        time = (target - pos) / spd
        stack.append(time)
        
        # 3. 如果当前车（后车）的时间 <= 前车的时间，说明追上了，合并车队
        # If current car (behind) time <= car ahead time, it catches up, merge fleet
        if len(stack) >= 2 and stack[-1] <= stack[-2]:
            stack.pop() # 弹出当前车（后车），保留前车的时间 / Pop current car, keep car ahead's time
            
    return len(stack) # 栈中剩余的元素个数就是车队数量 / Remaining elements are the number of fleets

复杂度 / Complexity:

- 时间 / Time: O(N log N) (排序 / Sorting), O(N) (遍历 / Traversal). Total: O(N log N).

- 空间 / Space: O(N) (栈和排序数组 / Stack and sorted array).

举一反三 / Connect to other problems:

- #739 Daily Temperatures: 寻找下一个更大的元素（单调递减栈）。/ Find next greater element (monotonic decreasing stack).

- #84 Largest Rectangle in Histogram: 寻找左右边界（单调递增栈）。/ Find left and right boundaries (monotonic increasing stack).

📚 参考文献 / References:

- [LeetCode #853 Car Fleet](https://leetcode.com/problems/car-fleet/)

- [NeetCode Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pr6T-3yB9RM)

🧒 ELI5 (Explain Like I'm 5):

把车排成一排，离终点近的在最前面。算算每辆车自己开到终点要多久。如果后面的车算出来的时间比前面的短，说明它开得快，会追上前面的车，然后只能跟着前面的车慢慢开（变成一个车队）。我们用一个栈来记录每个车队的时间，最后栈里有几个时间，就有几个车队！

Line up the cars, closest to the finish line first. Calculate how long each car takes to reach the finish line on its own. If a car behind has a shorter time than the car ahead, it means it's faster, will catch up, and then must follow slowly (forming a fleet). We use a stack to record the time of each fleet. The number of times left in the stack is the number of fleets!

🗣️ Soft Skills

🗣️ 软技能 / Soft Skills — Tell me about a time you successfully navigated organizational change

为什么这很重要？ / Why this matters:

在快速发展的科技公司中，唯一不变的就是变化（重组、技术栈迁移、优先级调整）。高级/专家工程师（Senior/Staff）需要展现出在混乱中找到方向、稳定团队并推动落地的能力。

In fast-paced tech companies, the only constant is change (re-orgs, tech stack migrations, shifting priorities). Senior/Staff engineers must show they can find direction in chaos, stabilize the team, and drive execution.

STAR 拆解 / STAR Breakdown:

- S (Situation): 描述一个具体的组织变革（例如：公司决定从单体架构迁移到微服务，或者你的团队被合并到另一个部门）。/ Describe a specific organizational change (e.g., migrating from monolith to microservices, or your team merging with another).

- T (Task): 你的任务是什么？（不仅是写代码，还包括沟通、规划、缓解团队焦虑）。/ What was your task? (Not just coding, but communication, planning, mitigating team anxiety).

- A (Action): 你采取了什么行动？（主动沟通、制定过渡计划、建立反馈机制）。/ What actions did you take? (Proactive communication, creating a transition plan, setting up feedback loops).

- R (Result): 结果如何？（平稳过渡、系统上线、团队士气恢复）。/ What was the result? (Smooth transition, system launch, team morale restored).

❌ 糟糕的回答 / Bad Answer:

“公司突然要换框架，我只能跟着学，然后把代码重写了一遍。虽然很烦，但我还是完成了。”

"The company suddenly wanted to switch frameworks, so I had to learn it and rewrite the code. It was annoying, but I got it done."

(被动接受，抱怨，没有展现领导力 / Passive acceptance, complaining, no leadership shown)

✅ 优秀的回答 / Good Answer:

“当公司决定从 AWS 迁移到 GCP 时，团队很焦虑。我主动组织了技术分享会，梳理了迁移的风险点，并制定了分阶段的迁移计划。我还与运维团队建立了每日同步机制，确保问题及时解决。最终我们提前两周完成了迁移，并且零故障。”

"When the company decided to migrate from AWS to GCP, the team was anxious. I proactively organized tech sharing sessions, identified migration risks, and created a phased plan. I also set up daily syncs with Ops to resolve issues quickly. We finished two weeks early with zero downtime."

(主动出击，稳定军心，跨团队协作 / Proactive, stabilizing the team, cross-team collaboration)

💡 Senior/Staff 提示 / Senior/Staff Tips:

- Focus on the "Why": 解释你如何理解并传达变革背后的商业逻辑。/ Explain how you understood and communicated the business logic behind the change.

- Manage Up and Down: 你不仅要安抚下属，还要向上管理预期。/ You must manage expectations up and soothe anxiety down.

🔑 核心收获 / Key Takeaways:

拥抱变化，成为团队的“稳定器”，而不是“抱怨者”。

Embrace change and be the "stabilizer" for the team, not the "complainer."

📚 参考文献 / References:

- [Navigating Organizational Change](https://hbr.org/topic/subject/change-management)

- [The Senior Engineer's Guide to Reorgs](https://lethain.com/how-to-survive-and-thrive-during-a-reorg/)

🧒 ELI5 (Explain Like I'm 5):

就像大家正在玩搭积木，突然老师说要换成拼图。有的小朋友会哭闹，但你站出来说：“别怕，我教大家怎么拼，我们一起拼个大城堡！”

It's like everyone is playing with blocks, and suddenly the teacher says we have to switch to puzzles. Some kids might cry, but you step up and say, "Don't worry, I'll show you how, let's build a big castle together!"

🤖 AI

🤖 AI — AI News Roundup

1. Google 街景化 AI / Google is Street View-ifying AI

Google 正在利用 AI 从航拍和卫星图像中提取洞察，或者将“充满想象力的场景锚定在现实世界中”。据报道，这可能对城市规划者非常有用，或者可以把宇宙飞船放在纽约地标前面。

Google is using new AI tools to unlock insights from aerial and satellite images or anchor "imaginative scenes in the real world." Reportedly, this could be highly useful for urban planners, or for putting spaceships in front of New York landmarks.

🔗 [Source: The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence)

2. Anthropic 的 Mythos 模型发现 271 个 Firefox 漏洞 / Anthropic's Mythos model finds 271 bugs in Firefox

Mozilla 首席技术官 Bobby Holley 表示，Anthropic 专注于网络安全的 AI 模型 Claude Mythos Preview 在 Firefox 150 中发现了 271 个漏洞，称其能力“丝毫不亚于”顶级安全研究人员。不过，Mozilla 也表示尚未发现“顶尖人类研究人员无法发现的漏洞”。

Anthropic's cybersecurity-focused AI model, Claude Mythos Preview, found 271 bugs in Firefox 150. Mozilla CTO Bobby Holley called it "every bit as capable" as top security researchers. Reassuringly, Mozilla hasn't "seen any bugs that couldn't have been found by an elite human researcher," either.

🔗 [Source: The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence)

3. Google 创始人要求工程师使用内部 AI 编程代理 / Google founder mandates engineers use internal AI coding agents

据报道，Google 联合创始人 Sergey Brin 在给 DeepMind 员工的备忘录中表示，“必须强制每位 Gemini 工程师使用内部代理来完成复杂的多步任务”。这似乎是为了在 AI 编程竞赛中追赶 Anthropic 的步伐。

According to reports, Google co-founder Sergey Brin said in a memo to DeepMind employees that "every Gemini engineer must be forced to use internal agents for complex, multistep tasks." This appears to be a move to catch up to Anthropic in the AI coding race.

🔗 [Source: The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence)

📚 参考文献 / References:

- [The Verge: AI News](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence)

🧒 ELI5 (Explain Like I'm 5):

AI 正在变得越来越聪明！它不仅能帮我们在地图上画出未来的城市，还能像超级侦探一样找出电脑程序里的错误。连发明 Google 的大老板都说，写代码的叔叔阿姨们必须学会用 AI 小助手来帮忙工作呢！

AI is getting smarter! It can not only help us draw future cities on maps but also act like a super detective finding mistakes in computer programs. Even the big boss who invented Google says the people who write code must learn to use AI helpers for their work!

Frontend

🎨 前端 / Frontend — Event Loop — Microtasks, Macrotasks, requestAnimationFrame

场景 / Real-world scenario:

你在做一个 dashboard，需要在一个复杂的计算后立即更新 UI，但发现页面卡死了，或者动画掉帧了。为什么？因为你可能阻塞了主线程，或者没有正确理解 JavaScript 的事件循环。

You're building a dashboard and need to update the UI immediately after a heavy calculation, but the page freezes or animations drop frames. Why? You might have blocked the main thread or misunderstood the JavaScript Event Loop.

核心概念 / Core Concept:

JavaScript 是单线程的，它通过事件循环 (Event Loop)来处理异步任务。

JavaScript is single-threaded and uses the Event Loop to handle asynchronous tasks.

执行顺序 / Execution Order:

1. 同步代码 (Synchronous code): 立即执行。/ Execute immediately.

2. 微任务 (Microtasks): 当前宏任务结束后，在浏览器渲染之前执行。例如：Promise.then、MutationObserver。/ Execute after the current macrotask, before browser rendering. E.g., Promise.then, MutationObserver.

3. 宏任务 (Macrotasks): 在下一次事件循环中执行。例如：setTimeout、setInterval、setImmediate (Node.js)、I/O、UI 渲染。/ Execute in the next event loop iteration. E.g., setTimeout, setInterval, setImmediate (Node.js), I/O, UI rendering.

4. requestAnimationFrame (rAF): 在浏览器下一次重绘之前执行，通常是每秒 60 次（约 16.6ms）。/ Execute before the next browser repaint, typically 60 times per second (~16.6ms).

代码示例 / Code Snippet:


console.log('1. 同步代码 / Sync');

setTimeout(() => {
  console.log('5. 宏任务 / Macrotask (setTimeout)');
}, 0);

Promise.resolve().then(() => {
  console.log('3. 微任务 / Microtask (Promise)');
});

requestAnimationFrame(() => {
  console.log('4. rAF (在下一次重绘前 / Before next repaint)');
});

console.log('2. 同步代码 / Sync');

猜猜输出什么？ / Quiz:

A) 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

B) 1, 5, 3, 4, 2

C) 1, 2, 3, 5, 4

D) 1, 3, 2, 4, 5

答案：A

常见误区 / Common Mistake:

- ❌ 用 setTimeout 做动画 (Using setTimeout for animations): setTimeout 不保证执行时间，可能会导致掉帧。/ setTimeout doesn't guarantee execution time, which can lead to dropped frames.

- ✅ 用 requestAnimationFrame 做动画 (Using rAF for animations): 浏览器会自动优化，保证动画流畅。/ The browser optimizes it automatically for smooth animations.

何时使用 / When to use:

- 微任务 (Microtasks): 需要在当前任务完成后立即执行，且不希望被渲染打断的操作（如状态更新后的副作用）。/ Operations that need to run immediately after the current task, without being interrupted by rendering (e.g., side effects after state updates).

- 宏任务 (Macrotasks): 可以稍后执行的低优先级任务（如定时器、网络请求回调）。/ Low-priority tasks that can run later (e.g., timers, network request callbacks).

- rAF: 任何涉及视觉更新或动画的操作。/ Any operation involving visual updates or animations.

📚 参考文献 / References:

- [MDN: Event Loop](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Event_loop)

- [Tasks, microtasks, queues and schedules](https://jakearchibald.com/2015/tasks-microtasks-queues-and-schedules/)

🧒 ELI5 (Explain Like I'm 5):

事件循环就像一个餐厅服务员。他先把你点好的菜端上来（同步代码），然后马上把桌子上的空盘子收走（微任务），接着去厨房看看有没有新做好的菜（宏任务）。如果餐厅要关门打扫了，他会在打扫前把最后一点活干完（rAF）。

The event loop is like a waiter. He serves the food you ordered right away (sync code), then immediately clears the empty plates from the table (microtasks), and then checks the kitchen for newly prepared dishes (macrotasks). If the restaurant is about to close for cleaning, he finishes the last bit of work before cleaning (rAF).

item.title: byte-by-byte — 2026-04-21
item.description:
🏗️ System Design

🏗️ 系统设计 / System Design — Day 28

Design a Chat System (WhatsApp/Slack)

> 难度 / Difficulty: Advanced | 阶段 / Phase: Growth | 预计阅读 / Read time: 3 min

🧠 真实场景 / Real-World Scenario

想象你在设计一个即时通讯系统，目标是支持 5亿用户，每天发送 500亿条消息（就像WhatsApp）。你的系统需要支持：一对一私聊、群组聊天（最多500人）、消息状态（已发送/已送达/已读）、在线状态显示、文件/图片传输。

Imagine you're designing a real-time messaging system to support 500M users with 50B messages/day (think WhatsApp). Requirements: 1:1 chat, group chat (up to 500 members), message status (sent/delivered/read), online presence, and file/media sharing.

📐 Architecture Overview


                        ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                        │          Client (Mobile/Web)         │
                        └──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                                       │ WebSocket (persistent)
                        ┌──────────────▼──────────────────────┐
                        │          API Gateway / LB            │
                        └──────┬──────────────┬───────────────┘
                               │              │
              ┌────────────────▼──┐    ┌──────▼──────────────┐
              │  Chat Service     │    │  Presence Service    │
              │  (WebSocket Mgr)  │    │  (Redis Pub/Sub)     │
              └────────┬──────────┘    └──────┬───────────────┘
                       │                      │
         ┌─────────────▼──────────┐    ┌──────▼───────────────┐
         │  Message Queue (Kafka) │    │  Redis (Online State)│
         └─────────────┬──────────┘    └──────────────────────┘
                       │
         ┌─────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
         │  Message Processor                          │
         │  - fan-out to recipients                    │
         │  - push notification if offline             │
         └───┬────────────────────────┬───────────────┘
             │                        │
    ┌────────▼──────────┐    ┌────────▼───────────────┐
    │  Message DB        │    │  Push Notification      │
    │  (Cassandra)       │    │  Service (APNs/FCM)     │
    └───────────────────┘    └────────────────────────┘

    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Media Service                                   │
    │  - S3 for storage, CDN for delivery             │
    │  - Pre-signed URLs for upload/download          │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

⚡ Key Design Decisions / 关键设计决策

#### 1. WebSocket vs HTTP Polling

用WebSocket，不用轮询。

WebSocket keeps a persistent bidirectional connection — ideal for real-time messaging. HTTP long-polling (Comet) works but wastes resources. Server-Sent Events (SSE) is one-way only.

选WebSocket的原因: 延迟低（< 100ms），服务器可主动推送，连接复用减少握手开销。

#### 2. Message Storage: Cassandra (not MySQL)

- 写入极重 (write-heavy): 每秒数百万条消息

- 按 (chat_id, message_id) 分区，天然支持时间范围查询

- 高可用，无单点故障

- Schema:


  CREATE TABLE messages (
    chat_id     UUID,
    message_id  TIMEUUID,   -- sortable by time
    sender_id   UUID,
    content     TEXT,
    type        TEXT,       -- 'text', 'image', 'file'
    status      TEXT,       -- 'sent', 'delivered', 'read'
    PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, message_id)
  ) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (message_id DESC);

#### 3. Message Fan-Out Strategy

For 1:1 chat: simple — push to recipient's WebSocket connection.

For group chat (up to 500 members): fan-out on write via Kafka.

- Message lands in Kafka topic

- Consumer service fans out to each member's inbox

- Why Kafka? Durability, replay, and decouples producers from consumers

群组消息扇出 (fan-out on write) vs 扇出读取 (fan-out on read):

Fan-out on write = 写入时复制到每人收件箱（适合中小群组）

Fan-out on read = 读取时聚合（适合超大群组/Twitter模式）

500人以内：写时扇出 — 读取延迟更低，体验更好。

#### 4. Online Presence

- Use Redis pub/sub per user channel

- Client sends heartbeat every 5s; server marks user online in Redis with TTL=10s

- Subscribe to friend's channel to receive presence updates

- 问题: 5亿用户在线状态 → Redis Cluster，按用户ID分片

❌ 别踩这些坑 / Common Mistakes

| ❌ 误区 | ✅ 正确做法 |

|---------|------------|

| 用MySQL存消息 | 用Cassandra/HBase — 写入QPS太高 |

| HTTP轮询实现"实时" | WebSocket长连接 |

| 同步fan-out到群成员 | 异步Kafka消费 |

| 不做消息去重 | 每条消息UUID + 客户端幂等性 |

| 媒体文件存数据库 | S3 + CDN + pre-signed URL |

| 忘记离线消息 | 推送通知 (APNs/FCM) + 消息持久化 |

🔢 Back-of-Envelope / 估算


DAU: 500M users
Messages per user per day: 40
Total messages/day: 20B
Peak QPS: 20B / 86400 * 2 (peak factor) ≈ 460K msg/s

Storage per message: ~100 bytes
Daily storage: 20B * 100 = 2TB/day
5-year retention: ~3.6PB (need compression + tiering)

WebSocket connections (peak): ~100M concurrent
→ Need ~10,000 chat servers (each handles ~10K connections)

📚 References

- [System Design Interview – WhatsApp](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vvhC64hQZMk) — Alex Xu walkthrough

- [How Discord Stores Billions of Messages](https://discord.com/blog/how-discord-stores-billions-of-messages) — Real Cassandra story

- [WhatsApp Architecture](https://highscalability.com/blog/2014/2/26/the-whatsapp-architecture-facebook-bought-for-19-billion.html) — HighScalability

🧒 ELI5

把聊天系统想成邮局：你发信（消息）→ 邮局（服务器）分拣 → 立刻送到收件人信箱（WebSocket）。如果收件人不在家（离线），就留张纸条（推送通知）让他回来取。Cassandra就像超大容量的信件档案室，永不丢信。

Think of it like a postal service: you drop a letter → post office (server) sorts it → delivers to recipient's mailbox instantly (WebSocket). If they're offline, leave a note (push notification). Cassandra is the giant mail archive that never loses a letter.

💻 Algorithms

💻 算法 / Algorithms — Day 28

#739 Daily Temperatures (Medium) — Stack Pattern (5/7)

> 模式 / Pattern: 单调栈 (Monotonic Stack) | 阶段 / Phase: Growth | 预计阅读 / Read time: 4 min

🧩 单调栈 (Monotonic Stack) — 5/7 — building on the template from Day 23 (Valid Parentheses), Day 24 (Min Stack), Day 26 (Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation)

今天是单调栈模式的第5题。前面我们用栈做了括号匹配、最小值追踪、表达式求值。今天进入单调栈最经典的用法：找下一个更大元素 (next greater element)。

Today is the 5th problem in the stack block. We've used stacks for parentheses, min tracking, and expression evaluation. Now we hit the most classic monotonic stack use case: finding the next greater element.

🔗 Links

- 🔗 [LeetCode #739](https://leetcode.com/problems/daily-temperatures/) 🟡 Medium

- 📹 [NeetCode Video](https://www.neetcode.io/problems/daily-temperatures)

🌍 Real-World Analogy / 现实类比

你站在一排人群中，每个人都想知道：后面什么时候会出现比我更高的人？

暴力解法：每个人回头一个个数。

聪明解法：维护一个"等待队列"——还没找到更高者的人先排队，一旦出现更高的，通知所有比他矮的人。

You're in a queue; each person wants to know: when will someone taller appear behind me?

Brute force: each person looks back one by one.

Smart: maintain a "waiting list" — those who haven't found someone taller yet wait in stack. When a taller person appears, notify everyone shorter.

📋 Problem


Input:  temperatures = [73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73]
Output: [1,  1,  4,  2,  1,  1,  0,  0]

For each day, find how many days until a warmer temperature. If none, return 0.

🗺️ Mapping to Pattern Template


# Template (from Day 22 intro):
# stack = []
# for i, num in enumerate(arr):
#     while stack and arr[stack[-1]] < num:
#         idx = stack.pop()
#         result[idx] = num  # next greater
#     stack.append(i)

# Daily Temperatures — direct application:
# arr = temperatures
# result[idx] = i - idx  (distance, not value)

这题 vs 模板的区别 / Difference from template:

- Template records the "next greater value" → this problem records the distance (i - idx)

- Everything else is identical: maintain decreasing stack of indices

✅ Solution with Trace


def dailyTemperatures(temperatures: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(temperatures)
    result = [0] * n
    stack = []  # stack of indices, temperatures[stack top] is always decreasing
    
    for i, temp in enumerate(temperatures):
        # Pop all indices where we found a warmer day
        while stack and temperatures[stack[-1]] < temp:
            prev_idx = stack.pop()
            result[prev_idx] = i - prev_idx  # days to wait
        stack.append(i)
    
    # Remaining indices in stack → no warmer day found, result stays 0
    return result

逐步追踪 / Step-by-step trace:


temperatures = [73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73]
index:          [0,  1,  2,  3,  4,  5,  6,  7 ]

i=0, temp=73: stack=[] → push 0.      stack=[0]
i=1, temp=74: 74>73(idx0)→result[0]=1; push 1.  stack=[1]
i=2, temp=75: 75>74(idx1)→result[1]=1; push 2.  stack=[2]
i=3, temp=71: 71<75 → just push 3.    stack=[2,3]
i=4, temp=69: 69<71 → just push 4.    stack=[2,3,4]
i=5, temp=72: 72>69(idx4)→result[4]=1
              72>71(idx3)→result[3]=2
              72<75 → stop, push 5.   stack=[2,5]
i=6, temp=76: 76>72(idx5)→result[5]=1
              76>75(idx2)→result[2]=4; push 6.   stack=[6]
i=7, temp=73: 73<76 → push 7.         stack=[6,7]

result = [1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0] ✓

⏱️ Complexity: Time O(n) — each element pushed/popped at most once. Space O(n).

🔄 举一反三 / Pattern Variations in This Block

| Problem | Stack Usage | What Changes |

|---------|------------|--------------|

| #20 Valid Parentheses (1/7) | matching brackets | pop on match |

| #155 Min Stack (2/7) | dual stack for min | track minimum |

| #150 Eval RPN (3/7) | operator/operand | pop two, compute |

| #739 Daily Temps (5/7) | monotonic decreasing | next greater |

| #853 Car Fleet (6/7) | monotonic | merge fleets |

| #84 Histogram (7/7) | monotonic | area calculation |

核心变体 / Core variation to recognize:

"Next greater/smaller" → monotonic stack (today's pattern)

"Matching/balanced" → bracket stack (Day 23)

"Evaluate expression" → operand/operator stack (Day 26)

📚 References

- [LeetCode Discussion — Best Explanation](https://leetcode.com/problems/daily-temperatures/solutions/109832/java-easy-ac-solution-with-stack/)

- [NeetCode — Monotonic Stack Explained](https://neetcode.io/courses/dsa-for-beginners/29)

- [Visualgo — Stack Visualization](https://visualgo.net/en/list)

🧒 ELI5

想象你在排队买票，每个人记录"我前面什么时候会有空位（比我快的人离开）"。我们维护一个"还在等的人"的列表，按顺序排。一旦有人离开（温度更高），就告诉所有等得比他久的人"你等了几天"。这样每个人最多进出列表一次，比一个个回头数快多了！

Imagine everyone in line tracking "when will someone faster than me appear?" We keep a list of people still waiting in order. When someone faster shows up, we notify everyone slower. Each person enters/leaves the list at most once — way faster than checking one by one!

🗣️ Soft Skills

🗣️ 软技能 / Soft Skills — Day 28

Build vs Buy Decision Making

> 难度 / Level: Senior/Staff | 类别 / Category: Decision Making | 预计阅读 / Read time: 2 min

🎯 为什么这个问题很重要 / Why This Question Matters

Build vs buy是每个Senior/Staff工程师都会遇到的战略决策。面试官想看：你会不会权衡短期成本 vs 长期维护，控制权 vs 速度，差异化价值 vs 通用功能。这不只是技术问题，更是工程判断力的体现。

Build vs buy is a strategic decision every Senior/Staff engineer faces. Interviewers want to see: can you weigh short-term cost vs long-term maintenance, control vs speed, differentiating value vs commodity functionality? This tests engineering judgment, not just technical skills.

⭐ STAR Framework

Situation / 背景:

> "我们在构建实时数据管道，需要一个消息队列。团队有人提议自研，也有人提议用Kafka。这是个200万用户的产品，但消息队列不是我们的核心竞争力。"

> "We were building a real-time data pipeline and needed a message queue. Some wanted to build one; others wanted Kafka. 2M users, but messaging wasn't our core differentiator."

Task / 任务:

> 评估两个方案的真实成本，给出有数据支撑的建议。

Action / 行动:

> 我做了一个快速分析框架：

> 1. 核心 vs 非核心 — 消息队列是通用基础设施，不是我们的差异化竞争力

> 2. 总拥有成本 (TCO) — 自研：3个工程师×6个月 + 永续维护。Kafka：2周集成 + 运维成本（~$500/月托管服务）

> 3. 风险矩阵 — 自研：稳定性风险、没有社区支持。Kafka：供应商依赖、少量定制限制

> 4. 团队能力 — 没有分布式系统专家，自研风险高

> I built a quick decision framework:

> 1. Core vs commodity — message queuing is generic infrastructure, not our differentiation

> 2. TCO — build: 3 engineers × 6 months + perpetual maintenance vs buy: 2-week integration + ~$500/month managed service

> 3. Risk matrix — build: stability risk, no community. Buy: vendor dependency, some customization limits

> 4. Team capabilities — no distributed systems experts on team

> 我建议采用托管Kafka（Confluent Cloud）。节省了约18个工程师月，让团队专注于产品功能。

Result / 结果:

> 集成用了两周，比预期早6个月上线。运行了1年没有重大故障。后来我把这个框架整理成团队的"Make vs Buy"决策模板，被多个团队复用。

> Integration took 2 weeks, shipped 6 months early. Zero major incidents in year one. I documented the framework as a team "Make vs Buy" template — adopted by 3 other teams.

❌ Bad Answer vs ✅ Good Answer

❌ 踩坑回答:

> "我们选择了Kafka因为它很流行，大家都在用。"

问题: 没有展示决策过程，没有权衡，听起来像随大流。

✅ 高分回答:

> "我建立了一个框架来分析核心竞争力、TCO和团队风险，然后带着数据向stakeholders推荐了Kafka。结果节省了18个工程师月，让我们更早交付了用户真正需要的功能。"

🚀 Senior/Staff级别加分点

1. 量化影响 — 不只说"省了时间"，要说"节省18个工程师月 = $X万美元"

2. 展示框架 — 面试官想看你有可复用的决策方法，不是ad-hoc

3. 考虑长期维护 — "我们今天能构建它，但谁来维护？"

4. 识别错误的build理由 — "我们想完全控制" → 通常是overengineering的信号

5. 何时应该build — 当功能是核心差异化价值，或有严格合规要求（数据主权），或外部方案有根本性gap

经典Build vs Buy框架:


Build when:
✅ Core differentiator (your competitive moat)
✅ Existing solutions have fundamental gaps
✅ Compliance/data sovereignty requirements
✅ Team has the expertise + bandwidth

Buy when:
✅ Commodity functionality
✅ No differentiation value
✅ High quality options exist
✅ Speed to market matters
✅ Team lacks domain expertise

💡 Key Takeaways / 核心要点

- 🎯 不要build ego trip — "因为自己写的更好" 不是理由

- 📊 TCO要算全 — 工程时间 + 机会成本 + 永续维护 + 招聘专才

- 🔑 核心竞争力优先 — 只在用户愿意为之付钱的差异化功能上build

- 📝 记录决策 — ADR (Architecture Decision Record) 让团队对齐，避免反复争论

📚 References

- [ADR (Architecture Decision Records) — Michael Nygard](https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions)

- [Build vs Buy Framework — a16z](https://a16z.com/build-vs-buy/)

- [Stop building commodity features — pragmatic engineering](https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/)

🧒 ELI5

自己造汽车还是买车？你要上班，开车去。你是汽车专家吗？不是。造车需要多久？1年。买车需要多久？1周。除非你是赛车手（汽车是你的核心竞争力），否则就买！工程决策也一样——把精力放在你做得比别人更好的地方。

Build a car or buy one? You need to get to work. Are you a car expert? No. How long to build? 1 year. Buy? 1 week. Unless you're a race car driver (cars ARE your competitive edge), just buy! Engineering is the same — spend your energy where you're uniquely better than others.

🤖 AI

🤖 AI — Day 28

MCP (Model Context Protocol) — The USB for AI

> 类别 / Category: Agents | 阶段 / Phase: Growth | 预计阅读 / Read time: 2 min

🧠 直觉解释 / Intuitive Explanation

想象你的电脑没有USB标准。每个设备都需要专用接口——鼠标一种、键盘一种、硬盘一种。你每次想接新设备都要改电脑硬件。这很蠢对吧？

MCP (Model Context Protocol) 就是AI工具的USB标准。

它由Anthropic于2024年底发布，解决了一个核心问题：AI模型（LLMs）如何以统一的方式连接到外部工具、数据库、API？以前每家公司都要自己写集成代码，现在有了MCP，任何AI应用都能"即插即用"地接入MCP服务器。

Imagine your computer had no USB standard. Every device needs a custom port. Annoying, right?

MCP is the USB standard for AI tools.

Released by Anthropic in late 2024, it solves a core problem: how can AI models connect to external tools, databases, and APIs in a unified way? Before MCP, every company wrote custom integration code. Now any AI app can "plug in" to any MCP server.

⚙️ How It Works / 工作原理


┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  MCP Architecture                    │
│                                                     │
│  ┌──────────────┐     MCP Protocol     ┌──────────┐ │
│  │  AI Host     │◄──────────────────►│ MCP      │ │
│  │  (Claude,    │   JSON-RPC over     │ Server   │ │
│  │   Cursor,    │   stdio / HTTP/SSE  │          │ │
│  │   Copilot)   │                     │ Exposes: │ │
│  └──────────────┘                     │ • Tools  │ │
│                                       │ • Resources│
│  MCP Client                          │ • Prompts │ │
│  (built into host)                   └──────────┘ │
│                                                     │
│  Examples of MCP Servers:                          │
│  • Filesystem (read/write local files)             │
│  • GitHub (search repos, create PRs)               │
│  • PostgreSQL (query databases)                    │
│  • Slack (send messages, search)                   │
│  • Brave Search (web search)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

三个核心原语 / Three Core Primitives:

1. Tools (工具) — Functions the AI can call (e.g., search_web, create_file)

2. Resources (资源) — Data the AI can read (e.g., file contents, database rows)

3. Prompts (提示词) — Reusable prompt templates exposed by the server

🐍 Runnable Python Example


# pip install mcp anthropic

from mcp.server import Server
from mcp.server.stdio import stdio_server
import mcp.types as types

# Build a minimal MCP server that exposes a weather tool
app = Server("weather-server")

@app.list_tools()
async def list_tools() -> list[types.Tool]:
    return [
        types.Tool(
            name="get_weather",
            description="Get current weather for a city",
            inputSchema={
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}
                },
                "required": ["city"]
            }
        )
    ]

@app.call_tool()
async def call_tool(name: str, arguments: dict) -> list[types.TextContent]:
    if name == "get_weather":
        city = arguments["city"]
        # In real code: call a weather API here
        return [types.TextContent(
            type="text",
            text=f"Weather in {city}: 72°F, sunny ☀️"
        )]

# Run the server (Claude Desktop can now connect to it!)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import asyncio
    asyncio.run(stdio_server(app))

Connect this to Claude Desktop via claude_desktop_config.json and Claude can now call get_weather as a native tool!

🌐 Applications / 应用场景

| Use Case | MCP Server |

|----------|-----------|

| AI reads/writes your codebase | Filesystem MCP |

| AI creates GitHub PRs | GitHub MCP |

| AI queries your database | PostgreSQL MCP |

| AI searches the web | Brave Search MCP |

| AI books calendar events | Google Calendar MCP |

| AI reads company docs | Notion/Confluence MCP |

为什么重要 / Why It Matters:

- 标准化 → 生态繁荣（类比：npm为JS，MCP为AI工具）

- 安全 → MCP服务器可控制权限，AI不能随意访问

- 可组合 → 一个AI客户端可同时接多个MCP服务器

⚡ MCP vs Function Calling

| | Function Calling | MCP |

|--|--|--|

| 标准化 | 各厂商自定义 | 统一协议 |

| 服务器端部署 | 不支持 | 支持 |

| 资源访问 | 无 | 支持 (Resources) |

| 跨模型兼容 | ❌ | ✅ |

📚 References

- [MCP Official Docs — Anthropic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction)

- [MCP GitHub Repo](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk)

- [Awesome MCP Servers](https://github.com/punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers)

🧒 ELI5

以前AI想用工具，就像每次换手机都要重新教它所有的按钮。MCP就是给AI装了个"学徒手册"：任何工具只要按格式写好，AI就能立刻会用，不用每次重新配置。就像学会了用筷子，就能夹任何菜。

Before MCP, teaching an AI a new tool was like rewriting the instruction manual every time. MCP is a standard instruction format — any tool written to spec can be used by any AI immediately. Like learning chopsticks: once you know the technique, you can pick up any food.

Frontend

🎨 前端 / Frontend — Day 28

Promises, async/await — Async Control Flow

> 类别 / Category: JavaScript Core | Week: 5 | 预计阅读 / Read time: 2 min

🌍 真实场景 / Real Scenario

你在做一个 dashboard，需要同时加载用户数据、最新订单、和通知列表。如果按顺序串行请求，会浪费 3x 时间。你需要理解 Promise 并发控制 才能写出生产级的异步代码。

You're building a dashboard that needs to load user profile, latest orders, and notifications. Sequential requests waste 3x the time. Understanding Promise concurrency control is essential for production-grade async code.

🧪 猜猜输出什么？ / What does this output?


async function fetchDashboard(userId: string) {
  console.log("A");
  
  const user = await fetch(`/api/users/${userId}`);
  console.log("B");
  
  const [orders, notifications] = await Promise.all([
    fetch(`/api/orders?userId=${userId}`),
    fetch(`/api/notifications?userId=${userId}`)
  ]);
  console.log("C");
  
  return { user, orders, notifications };
}

fetchDashboard("123");
console.log("D");

What logs first?

- A) A → B → C → D

- B) A → D → B → C

- C) D → A → B → C

- D) A → B → D → C

> 答案 / Answer: B — async functions run synchronously until the first await. So "A" logs, then the function suspends at await fetch(...), and "D" logs immediately. When the fetch resolves, "B" logs, then "C" after Promise.all.

🔑 Core Concepts

#### Promise 状态机 / Promise State Machine


pending → fulfilled (resolve)
        → rejected  (reject)

Once settled, state never changes.

#### 三种并发模式 / Three Concurrency Patterns


// ❌ Pattern 1: Sequential (串行) — SLOW
const user = await fetchUser(id);      // waits 200ms
const orders = await fetchOrders(id);  // waits another 300ms
// Total: 500ms — unnecessary!

// ✅ Pattern 2: Parallel (并行) — FAST
const [user, orders] = await Promise.all([
  fetchUser(id),    // both start at the same time
  fetchOrders(id),  // 
]);
// Total: max(200ms, 300ms) = 300ms 🚀

// ⚠️ Pattern 3: Promise.allSettled — when you need ALL results
// even if some fail (e.g., non-critical widgets)
const results = await Promise.allSettled([
  fetchUser(id),
  fetchOrders(id),
  fetchNotifications(id),
]);
results.forEach(r => {
  if (r.status === 'fulfilled') console.log(r.value);
  else console.error(r.reason);
});

❌ Common Mistakes / 常见错误


// ❌ Mistake 1: await inside map() — sequential, not parallel
const data = await Promise.all(
  ids.map(id => await fetchUser(id))  // SyntaxError! can't await inside non-async map
);

// ✅ Correct: pass Promise directly
const data = await Promise.all(
  ids.map(id => fetchUser(id))  // no await inside map
);

// ❌ Mistake 2: unhandled rejection
const result = await Promise.all([fetchA(), fetchB()]); // if B rejects, A's result lost!

// ✅ Correct: use allSettled or try/catch per request
const [a, b] = await Promise.allSettled([fetchA(), fetchB()]);

// ❌ Mistake 3: missing error handling
async function loadData() {
  const data = await fetchData(); // throws? crashes silently!
  return data;
}

// ✅ Correct:
async function loadData() {
  try {
    return await fetchData();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("Failed to load:", err);
    return null; // or throw to parent
  }
}

🎯 When to Use / When NOT to Use


Use Promise.all when:
✅ All requests are independent
✅ You need ALL to succeed (fail fast if any fails)
✅ Performance matters (dashboard loads, batch ops)

Use Promise.allSettled when:
✅ Some failures are acceptable
✅ Non-critical widgets/sections
✅ You need all results regardless of failure

Use sequential await when:
✅ Request B depends on result of A
✅ Ordering matters (database transactions)
✅ You need to avoid rate limiting

Avoid:
❌ await in a for loop when items are independent
❌ new Promise() wrapping async functions (anti-pattern)
❌ .then() chains when async/await is available (less readable)

🔥 Production Pattern: TypeScript async with error handling


type Result<T> = { data: T; error: null } | { data: null; error: Error };

async function safeAsync<T>(promise: Promise<T>): Promise<Result<T>> {
  try {
    const data = await promise;
    return { data, error: null };
  } catch (err) {
    return { data: null, error: err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)) };
  }
}

// Usage — no try/catch needed at call site:
const { data: user, error } = await safeAsync(fetchUser("123"));
if (error) return <ErrorState message={error.message} />;

📚 References

- [MDN — Promise](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise)

- [MDN — async/await](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/JavaScript/Asynchronous/Promises)

- [JavaScript.info — Promise API](https://javascript.info/promise-api)

🧒 ELI5

Promise就像点外卖的收据。你点了3个菜（3个请求）。串行 = 等第一个菜上了再点第二个，太慢。Promise.all = 同时点3个菜，哪个先好哪个先上，全部好了再吃。allSettled = 就算有菜没做出来，你也能知道哪些成功了哪些失败了。

A Promise is like a takeout receipt. You ordered 3 dishes. Sequential = wait for dish 1 before ordering dish 2 (slow!). Promise.all = order all 3 at once, eat when all are ready. allSettled = even if one fails, you know which succeeded and which didn't.

item.description:
🏗️ System Design

📊 NeetCode: 23/150 · SysDesign: 22/40 · Behavioral: 22/40 · Frontend: 22/50 · AI: 11/30

🔥 1-day streak!

🏗️ 系统设计 / System Design

设计新闻流（Twitter / Facebook）/ Design a News Feed

1) 场景 / Scenario

想象你在做一个社交 App：

- 用户关注很多人

- 打开首页要看到“关注的人最新动态”（按时间倒序）

- 需要：快速打开、可无限下拉、支持发帖/删帖、支持隐私（拉黑/仅好友）

You’re building a social app:

- Users follow many accounts

- Home timeline shows recent posts from followees (reverse chronological)

- Requirements: fast load, infinite scroll, post/delete, privacy (blocks / friends-only)

2) 关键 API / Core APIs

- POST /posts 创建动态 / create post

- POST /follow 关注 / follow

- GET /feed?cursor=... 拉取首页流 / fetch feed

- DELETE /posts/{id} 删除动态 / delete

3) 两种主流方案 / Two common approaches

A. Fanout-on-write（写入时推送）

发帖时把这条 post “复制/投递”到所有粉丝的 inbox/feed 存储。

Pros:

- 读快：GET /feed 只扫自己的 inbox

Cons:

- 写放大：大 V 发帖会写爆

- 需要异步队列 + 回压

B. Fanout-on-read（读取时拉取）

读首页时：查自己关注列表 → 拉取每个关注者的最近 posts → 合并排序（k-way merge）。

Pros:

- 写轻：发帖只写一份

Cons:

- 读慢：关注很多人时合并开销大

- 需要缓存/预计算

现实里通常是 混合：普通用户 fanout-on-write；大 V / 名人用 fanout-on-read 或“部分推送”。

In practice it’s hybrid: push for normal users; pull (or partial push) for celebrities.

4) 推荐架构（混合）/ Suggested architecture (Hybrid)


          +-------------------+
Client -->|  API Gateway      |
          +---------+---------+
                    |
          +---------v---------+
          |  Feed Service     |<-------------------+
          +----+---------+----+                    |
               |         |                         |
   (read path) |         | (write path)            |
               |         v                         |
        +------v--+   +--+----------------+        |
        |  Cache  |   |  Post Service     |        |
        | (Redis) |   +--+----------------+        |
        +----+----+      |                         |
             |           v                         |
             |     +-----+------+                  |
             |     |  Post Store | (Cassandra/LSM)  |
             |     +-----+------+                  |
             |           |                         |
             |           v                         |
             |     +-----+------+      +-----------+--------+
             |     |  MQ / Log  |----->| Fanout Workers     |
             |     | (Kafka)    |      | (async push)       |
             |     +------------+      +-----------+--------+
             |                                     |
             |                                     v
             |                           +---------+--------+
             +-------------------------->|  Inbox Store      |
                                         | (per user feed)   |
                                         +------------------+

关键点 / Key ideas:

- Post Store：存权威 post（可按 authorId + time 索引）

- Inbox Store：每个用户一个“收件箱时间线”（只存 postId + ts + authorId）

- MQ：解耦发帖与推送；可重放、可扩容

- Cache：热点用户首页、关注列表、作者最新 posts

5) 读路径 / Read path (GET /feed)

1. 先查 Redis：是否有缓存的第一页（或 cursor 对应页）

2. 没命中：从 Inbox Store 取 N 条（按时间倒序），拿到 postIds

3. 批量去 Post Store / Cache 取 post 内容（MGET / batch)

4. 过滤隐私（block / friends-only）并返回

Cursor 设计：用 (lastTimestamp, lastPostId) 做稳定翻页，避免 offset 分页在插入/删除时乱跳。

6) 写路径 / Write path (POST /posts)

1. 写入 Post Store（生成 snowflake/UUID）

2. 投递事件到 Kafka：PostCreated(postId, authorId, ts)

3. Fanout worker：

- 取 author 的 followers

- 对普通作者：批量写入 followers 的 Inbox Store

- 对大 V：不 fanout（只写作者自己的 “author timeline”）

7) 关键取舍 / Key tradeoffs

- 读延迟 vs 写放大：push 读快但写爆；pull 写轻但读慢

- 一致性：首页允许 eventual consistency（秒级延迟可接受）

- 存储成本：inbox 只存指针（postId），否则成本爆炸

- 名人策略：按 follower 数阈值切换策略（并动态调整）

8) 常见坑 / Common mistakes

- 只做 fanout-on-write：遇到“大 V”直接写入风暴

- Inbox 存全量 post 内容：重复数据导致存储/回填困难

- 用 offset 分页：新帖插入后翻页错乱、重复/漏读

- 忽视隐私与删除：需要支持“撤回/删除”传播（tombstone + read-time filter）

🧒 ELI5

把新闻流想成“报纸投递”：

- 推送：作者一发文章，就把报纸送到每个订阅者门口（读很快，但送货很累）。

- 拉取：你想看时自己去每个作者家门口拿最新报纸，再拼成一份（写很轻，但你得跑很多家）。

所以现实里：普通作者直接投递；大明星让你来取。

📚 References

- https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/system-design/answer-keys/design-twitter

- https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/system-design/answer-keys/design-facebook-news-feed

- https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/

💻 Algorithms

📊 NeetCode: 23/150 · SysDesign: 22/40 · Behavioral: 22/40 · Frontend: 22/50 · AI: 11/30

🔥 1-day streak!

💻 算法 / Algorithms — #22 Generate Parentheses (Medium) — Stack

🧩 Stack (4/7) — building on the template from Day 1

今天这题和“括号匹配 / Valid Parentheses”同属一类：用栈表示“当前还没闭合的结构”。不同点是：

- Valid Parentheses 是“验证”

- Generate Parentheses 是“生成所有合法结果”

Today is in the same family as Valid Parentheses: use a stack to represent “currently open structures”. Difference:

- Valid Parentheses = verify

- Generate Parentheses = generate all valid sequences

🔗 LeetCode: https://leetcode.com/problems/generate-parentheses/ 🟡

📹 NeetCode: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s9fokUqJ76A

1) 现实类比 / Real-world analogy

把它想成写代码时的“自动补全括号”功能：你打了 (，编辑器知道你欠一个 )；但为了不出错，任何时候都不能让 ) 的数量超过 (。

Think of an editor auto-completing parentheses: every ( creates a debt of ); you can never close more than you opened.

2) 问题重述 / Restate

给定 n 对括号，生成所有长度 2n 的字符串，使得任意前缀里 ( 数量 ≥ ) 数量，且最终 ( == )。

Given n pairs, generate all length-2n strings such that for every prefix, opens ≥ closes, and total opens == closes.

3) 映射到模式 / Map to the pattern

这里的“栈”不一定真的要存字符（也可以只用计数），关键是它代表：

- stack 里有多少个“还没关掉的左括号”

So the “stack” conceptually is the number of unmatched (.

生成规则（约束驱动）：

- 还能放 (：当 open < n

- 还能放 )：当 close < open（否则会出现非法前缀）

4) Python 解法（回溯 + 栈含义）/ Python solution (Backtracking)


from typing import List

class Solution:
    def generateParenthesis(self, n: int) -> List[str]:
        res: List[str] = []

        def dfs(open_cnt: int, close_cnt: int, path: List[str]) -> None:
            # open_cnt: number of '(' used
            # close_cnt: number of ')' used
            # stack size == open_cnt - close_cnt (unmatched opens)
            if open_cnt == n and close_cnt == n:
                res.append(''.join(path))
                return

            # Option 1: add '(' if we still can
            if open_cnt < n:
                path.append('(')
                dfs(open_cnt + 1, close_cnt, path)
                path.pop()

            # Option 2: add ')' only if it won't break validity
            if close_cnt < open_cnt:
                path.append(')')
                dfs(open_cnt, close_cnt + 1, path)
                path.pop()

        dfs(0, 0, [])
        return res

小 trace / Mini trace (n=3)

- start: open=0 close=0 path=""

- add "(": open=1 close=0 path="("

- add "(": open=2 close=0 path="(("

- add ")": open=2 close=1 path="(()" ✅（因为 close < open）

- ...

核心：任何时刻都保证 close_cnt <= open_cnt，这等价于“栈从不变成负数”。

Key: maintain close_cnt <= open_cnt always (stack never negative).

5) 复杂度 / Complexity

- 时间：输出规模主导，结果数是第 n 个 Catalan 数 C_n，大约 O(C_n * n)（每个字符串长度 2n）

- 空间：递归深度 O(n) + 输出

Time is output-dominated: ~O(C_n * n). Space O(n) (excluding output).

6) 举一反三（同一模式块）/ Transfer (same pattern block)

- #20 Valid Parentheses：栈匹配（验证）

- #150 Evaluate RPN：栈求值（表达式）

- #739 Daily Temperatures：单调栈（找下一个更大元素）

- #84 Largest Rectangle：单调栈（结算区间）

同一个“Stack”家族里，核心都是：把“未完成的东西”压栈，遇到触发条件就出栈结算。

Across the Stack family, the idea is: push unfinished work, pop when a condition resolves it.

🧒 ELI5

你在搭积木：

- 放 ( 就像搭一层楼

- 放 ) 就像关掉一层楼

规则是：你不能先关楼再建楼，所以 ) 只能在已经有没关的 ( 时出现。

Like building floors: you can’t close a floor that wasn’t opened.

📚 References

- https://leetcode.com/problems/generate-parentheses/

- https://neetcode.io/problems/generate-parentheses

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_number

🗣️ Soft Skills

📊 NeetCode: 23/150 · SysDesign: 22/40 · Behavioral: 22/40 · Frontend: 22/50 · AI: 11/30

🔥 1-day streak!

🗣️ 软技能 / Soft Skills

如何在新团队建立信任？/ How do you build trust with a new team?

为什么重要 / Why this matters

中文：在新团队里，信任不是“人好就有”，而是一个降低协作摩擦的系统：大家相信你会按时交付、沟通透明、在关键时刻站得住。

English: Trust reduces coordination cost. People rely on you to deliver, communicate clearly, and act predictably under pressure.

STAR 拆解 / STAR breakdown

S (Situation)

中文：刚加入团队/跨组接手一个服务，代码和 ownership 都不熟，大家担心你会“乱改”。

English: You join a new team or inherit a service; ownership is unclear and people fear risky changes.

T (Task)

中文：在不打扰团队节奏的前提下，快速形成可靠产出，并让关键同事愿意与你协作。

English: Become productive without disrupting flow, and earn collaboration from key partners.

A (Action)

中文（可直接照着说，偏 Senior/Staff）：

1. 先对齐“成功定义”：1:1 问清楚本季度最重要的指标、风险点、谁是决策者。

2. 用小而稳的交付建立信用：先做一两个低风险改动（修 bug、补监控、改善 oncall runbook），在 PR 里解释“为什么”。

3. 默认透明：写 short design doc / RFC，记录 tradeoff；在 standup 里讲进展 + 阻塞 + 下一步。

4. 让别人更容易跟你合作：缩短 review turnaround；把复杂问题拆成可并行的 task；把“需要谁决定什么”写清楚。

5. 遇到问题先扛责再复盘：出事故时先稳定系统、同步影响面，再做 blameless postmortem。

English:

1. Align on what “success” means (metrics, risks, decision makers).

2. Build credibility with small, low-risk wins (bugfixes, monitoring, runbooks) and explain the “why” in PRs.

3. Default to transparency (short RFCs, tradeoffs, steady status updates).

4. Make collaboration easy (fast reviews, parallelizable tasks, explicit decisions needed).

5. In incidents: stabilize first, communicate clearly, then run a blameless postmortem.

R (Result)

中文：你会得到两类信任：

- 执行力信任（你说到做到）

- 判断力信任（你做的选择是靠谱的）

English: You earn both execution trust (you deliver) and judgment trust (your decisions are sound).

❌ Bad vs ✅ Good（示例回答对比）/ Bad vs Good

❌ 中文：

“我会多和大家沟通，努力融入团队。”（太空、不可验证）

✅ 中文：

“前两周我先做两件事：补齐关键指标监控 + 写 oncall runbook，并在每个 PR 里把风险和 rollback 写清楚。第三周开始我会发一个 1 页的 feed latency 优化 RFC，列出 2 个方案和 tradeoff，请 tech lead 做决策。”

❌ English:

“I communicate a lot and try to fit in.” (vague)

✅ English:

“In the first two weeks I shipped monitoring + an oncall runbook, and every PR included risk + rollback. In week three I proposed a 1-page latency RFC with two options and tradeoffs for the TL to decide.”

Senior / Staff 加分点 / Senior/Staff tips

- 中文：把信任当成 SLO：可预测的节奏（updates、designs、rollbacks）就是可靠性。

- 中文：用“决策日志”建立判断力：记录你为什么选 A 不选 B，半年后复盘你是否在提升。

- English: Treat trust like an SLO: predictable cadence beats charisma.

- English: Keep a decision log to demonstrate and improve judgment.

Key Takeaways

- 中文：信任=可预测 + 透明 + 稳定交付。

- 中文：先小胜建立信用，再啃硬骨头。

- English: Trust = predictability + transparency + delivery.

- English: Start with small wins, then tackle the hard problems.

🧒 ELI5

中文：你刚加入新班级，大家不认识你。你先按时交作业、说话算数、遇到问题会解释清楚，大家自然就信你。

English: In a new class, you earn trust by doing what you say, on time, and explaining things clearly.

📚 References

- https://staffeng.com/guides/staff-archetypes/

- https://www.pmcouncil.org/insights/psychological-safety/

- https://hbr.org/2019/01/the-fundamental-attribution-error

🤖 AI

📊 NeetCode: 23/150 · SysDesign: 22/40 · Behavioral: 22/40 · Frontend: 22/50 · AI: 11/30

🔥 1-day streak!

🤖 AI 动态 / AI News

📰 本周 AI 要闻 / This Week in AI

1. Sergey Brin：Google 要向 Anthropic 的编码智能体学习

据报道，Google 联合创始人 Sergey Brin 在内部备忘录中写道，Google 工程师必须强制使用内部 AI 智能体完成复杂任务，因为 Anthropic 的编码工具目前领先。他还暗示，赶上 Anthropic 是迈向"AI 自我改进"的一步。

According to reports, Google co-founder Sergey Brin wrote in an internal memo that every Gemini engineer "must be forced to use internal agents for complex, multistep tasks." Brin reportedly said Anthropic's coding tools are currently leading the race, and catching up is a step toward building AI that can improve itself.

🔗 [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence) · [The Information原报道](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-creates-strike-team-improve-coding-models)

2. Anthropic 发布 Claude Design（Opus 4.7 驱动）

Anthropic 推出 Claude Design，基于最新的 Opus 4.7 模型，允许用户创建设计稿、原型、Pitch Deck 和营销素材。目前在付费用户中以研究预览版开放。

Anthropic launched Claude Design — powered by Claude Opus 4.7 — letting users create designs, prototypes, pitch decks, and marketing materials. Available in research preview for paying subscribers.

🔗 [The Verge 报道](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/913184/anthropic-claude-opus-4-7-cybersecurity)

3. AI 影响力账号涌入社交媒体

据纽约时报调查，Instagram、TikTok、Facebook 上出现了数百个 AI 生成的假账号，疑似服务于政治目的。随着 AI 生成头像的成本大幅降低，批量创建虚假影响力账号变得前所未有的容易。

The New York Times found hundreds of AI-generated fake accounts across Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook, reportedly pushing political messaging. Experts note that creating such avatars is increasingly cheap and easy, with entire contractor networks specializing in bulk AI avatar deployment.

🔗 [The Verge 报道](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence)

🧒 ELI5

AI 这周：Google 承认落后了，Anthropic 出了个"AI 设计师"，社交媒体上 AI 假人越来越多也越来越便宜。

Google admitted it's behind on AI coding agents, Anthropic shipped an AI designer tool, and fake AI social media accounts are getting cheaper and easier to deploy at scale.

📚 References:

- https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence

- https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-creates-strike-team-improve-coding-models

Frontend

📊 NeetCode: 23/150 · SysDesign: 22/40 · Behavioral: 22/40 · Frontend: 22/50 · AI: 11/30

🔥 1-day streak!

🎨 前端 / Frontend

Closures & Lexical Scope — JS Interview Classic

场景 / Scenario

中文：你在做一个 dashboard，需要给每一行渲染一个“重试 / Retry”按钮。点击时要带上该行的 rowId。如果你不小心写错闭包，你可能会发现：不管点哪个按钮，拿到的都是同一个 rowId（通常是最后一个）。

English: You’re building a dashboard with a “Retry” button per row. If you misuse closures, every button can end up using the same rowId (often the last one).

核心概念 / Core idea

中文：

- 词法作用域（lexical scope）：变量能否被访问，取决于代码“写在哪里”，不是“从哪里调用”。

- 闭包（closure）：函数 + 它创建时捕获的外部变量环境。

English:

- Lexical scope: what you can access depends on where code is written, not where it’s called.

- Closure: a function plus the environment it captured when created.

代码示例 / Code snippet


// The closure captures `rowId`.
export function makeRetryHandler(rowId: string) {
  return async function onRetryClick() {
    // Comments in English
    await fetch(`/api/retry?rowId=${encodeURIComponent(rowId)}`, { method: 'POST' });
  };
}

// Usage (e.g., inside a component render)
const handler = makeRetryHandler(row.id);

中文：makeRetryHandler 返回的内部函数，会把 rowId “记住”。这就是闭包。

English: The inner function “remembers” rowId — that’s a closure.

猜猜输出什么？/ Quiz (A/B/C/D)


const fns: Array<() => number> = [];
for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
  fns.push(() => i);
}
console.log(fns[0](), fns[1](), fns[2]());

A) 0 1 2

B) 3 3 3

C) 0 0 0

D) 抛异常 / throws

答案 / Answer: B

中文解释：var 是函数作用域，循环结束后 i 变成 3；三个函数闭包捕获的是“同一个 i”。

English: var is function-scoped; after the loop i === 3, and all closures reference the same i.

常见错误 vs 正确写法 / Common mistake vs correct

❌ 错误（捕获同一个变量）/ Wrong:


const fns: Array<() => number> = [];
for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
  fns.push(() => i);
}

✅ 正确 1：用 let（块级作用域）/ Correct 1: use let:


const fns: Array<() => number> = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
  fns.push(() => i);
}

✅ 正确 2：用工厂函数制造新作用域 / Correct 2: scope factory:


const fns: Array<() => number> = [];
for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
  const fn = ((x: number) => () => x)(i);
  fns.push(fn);
}

什么时候用 / 什么时候别用 / When to use / when NOT to

中文（实战判断）：

- ✅ 用闭包：

- 你需要“绑定参数”给回调（事件处理、定时器、重试函数、日志上下文）

- 你需要封装内部状态（不想暴露成全局/类字段）

- ❌ 小心闭包：

- 在热路径里创建大量闭包（每次 render 都 new 很多函数）→ 可能导致子组件重复渲染

- 闭包捕获了会变化的大对象（例如 props/state 的整个对象）→ 容易产生“旧值 / stale value”问题

English (practical):

- ✅ Use closures to bind parameters to callbacks or to encapsulate private state.

- ⚠️ Be careful when creating tons of closures on hot render paths, or capturing changing objects that can cause stale values.

小提示（React/TS 实战）/ React/TS production tip

中文：如果你把 handler 传给 React.memo 子组件，并且不想每次 render 都变引用：

- 用 useCallback，并确保依赖是最小的（不要把整个对象塞进去）。

English: If passing handlers to memoized children, use useCallback with minimal dependencies.

🧒 ELI5

中文：闭包就像你把一个小纸条（变量）塞进函数口袋里。以后不管函数走到哪儿，都能掏出纸条看。

English: A closure is a function carrying a note in its pocket.

📚 References

- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Closures

- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Lexical_scope

- https://react.dev/reference/react/useCallback

Week Review

📅 Week in Review — Week 16 (10 min read)

📊 NeetCode: 23/150 · SysDesign: 22/40 · Behavioral: 22/40 · Frontend: 22/50 · AI: 11/30

🔥 26-day streak!

🗓️ This Week's Journey / 本周回顾

- Monday (Day 22): Unique ID Generators, Sliding Window Maximum, Process Improvement, TS Basics, Prompt Engineering. / 唯一 ID 生成器，滑动窗口最大值，流程改进，TS 基础，提示工程。

- Tuesday (Day 23): Web Crawlers, Valid Parentheses, Designing for Scale, TS with React, AI News. / 网络爬虫，有效括号，为扩展性设计，React+TS，AI 新闻。

- Wednesday (Day 24): Notification Systems, Min Stack, Conflict Resolution, TS Utility Types, Chain of Thought. / 通知系统，最小栈，冲突解决，TS 工具类型，思维链。

- Thursday (Day 25): Review Day — Consolidating the week's learnings. / 复习日 — 巩固本周所学。

- Friday (Day 26): Autocomplete Systems, Evaluate RPN, Handling Tough Feedback, TS Generics Deep Dive, AI Agents. / 自动补全系统，逆波兰表达式求值，应对严厉反馈，TS 泛型深度解析，AI 智能体。

- Saturday (Deep Dive): Designing a News Feed (Push vs Pull models). / 深度解析：设计信息流（推/拉模式）。

🧠 System Design: Key Takeaways / 系统设计要点

1. Distributed Coordination (分布式协调): From Snowflake IDs (no coordination) to Web Crawlers (Bloom filters for deduplication), avoiding centralized bottlenecks is key. / 从 Snowflake ID（无需协调）到网络爬虫（使用 Bloom Filter 去重），避免中心化瓶颈是关键。

2. Asynchronous Processing (异步处理): Notification systems rely heavily on message queues (Kafka/SQS) to decouple producers from consumers and ensure high availability. / 通知系统严重依赖消息队列（Kafka/SQS）来解耦生产者和消费者，确保高可用性。

3. Data Structures at Scale (规模化数据结构): Autocomplete relies on Tries with precomputed Top-K results at each node to guarantee <100ms latency. / 自动补全依赖 Trie 树，并在每个节点预计算 Top-K 结果以保证 <100ms 的延迟。

💻 Algorithms: Patterns Mastered / 算法模式总结

- Sliding Window Finale (滑动窗口收官): Mastered Monotonic Deque for Sliding Window Maximum (#239) — maintaining a decreasing queue of indices. / 掌握了用于滑动窗口最大值的单调队列——维护递减的索引队列。

- Stack Pattern (栈模式): Transitioned to Stacks. Solved Valid Parentheses (#20) for matching, Min Stack (#155) by augmenting elements with min_so_far, and Evaluate RPN (#150) for operand evaluation. / 转向栈模式。解决了有效括号（匹配）、最小栈（携带辅助信息）和逆波兰表达式求值（操作数计算）。

- Key Insight (核心洞察): Stacks are perfect for "lazy evaluation" — deferring processing until you have enough information (like matching a closing bracket or evaluating an operator). / 栈非常适合“延迟处理”——直到有足够信息（如匹配右括号或计算运算符）才进行处理。

🗣️ Soft Skills: What to Practice / 软技能练习重点

- Scenarios Covered: Process improvement, designing for scale, conflict resolution, and receiving tough feedback. / 涵盖场景：流程改进，扩展性设计，冲突解决，接受严厉反馈。

- What Needs Practice: Transitioning from "I built this" to "I influenced the team to build this." Emphasize data-driven decisions, gathering buy-in (RFCs/ADRs), and showing a growth mindset when facing criticism. / 需要练习：从“我做了这个”转变为“我影响团队做了这个”。强调数据驱动决策、获得团队认可（RFC/ADR）以及在面对批评时展现成长型思维。

🎨 Frontend: Concepts to Lock In / 前端知识巩固

- TypeScript Mastery: Moved from basic Types/Interfaces to using Generics for reusable logic. / 从基础的 Types/Interfaces 进阶到使用泛型实现逻辑复用。

- React Integration: Properly typing Props, Events (React.ChangeEvent), and Refs (useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)). / 正确为 Props、事件和 Refs 添加类型。

- Advanced TS: Leveraged Utility Types (Partial, Pick, Omit) to keep code DRY, and Type Guards (is keyword) for safe union type narrowing. Built a type-safe API client using Generics. / 利用工具类型保持代码 DRY，使用类型守卫安全缩小联合类型。使用泛型构建了类型安全的 API 客户端。

🤖 AI: What Stuck / AI 知识点

- Prompt Engineering & CoT: "Let's think step by step" forces the LLM to break down complex problems, improving reasoning accuracy. / “让我们一步一步思考”强迫大语言模型拆解复杂问题，提高推理准确率。

- AI Agents (ReAct): Agents combine Reasoning and Acting (Goal → Think → Act → Observe). They use tools to interact with the external world. / 智能体结合了推理与行动。它们使用工具与外部世界交互。

- Industry News: 据报道，联合国强调人类必须处于 AI 决策中心；美国多州推进 AI 立法（要求披露聊天机器人身份）；PwC 报告指出领先公司正利用 AI 重塑工作流而非仅仅添加工具。 / According to reports, the UN emphasizes humans must remain central to AI decisions; US states are advancing AI legislation; PwC reports leading companies are reinventing workflows with AI.

⚠️ What to Review / 需要复习的内容

- Stack Pop Order: In Evaluate RPN, remember that a - b means popping b first, then a. / 在逆波兰表达式求值中，记住 a - b 意味着先弹出 b，再弹出 a。

- System Design Tradeoffs: Review when to use pull vs. push models in News Feeds, especially handling the "Celebrity Problem". / 复习在信息流中何时使用拉模式 vs 推模式，特别是处理“明星问题”。

🏆 Win of the Week / 本周亮点

- Successfully transitioned from Sliding Window to Stack patterns, and built a fully type-safe API client in TypeScript! / 成功从滑动窗口模式过渡到栈模式，并在 TypeScript 中构建了完全类型安全的 API 客户端！

🎯 Next Week Preview / 下周预告

- Algorithms: Continuing the Stack pattern block (Generate Parentheses, Daily Temperatures). / 继续栈模式（生成括号，每日温度）。

- System Design: More distributed system components and data-heavy architectures. / 更多分布式系统组件和重数据架构。

- Frontend: Deepening React patterns and performance optimization. / 深化 React 模式和性能优化。

item.description:
Deepdive

🔬 Saturday Deep Dive: Design a News Feed (Twitter/Facebook) (15 min read)

📊 NeetCode: 23/150 · SysDesign: 22/40 · Behavioral: 22/40 · Frontend: 22/50 · AI: 11/30

🔥 26-day streak!

Overview / 概述

Designing a news feed is a classic system design interview question. It tests your ability to handle massive scale, balance read/write heavy workloads, and make trade-offs between latency and consistency.

设计信息流（News Feed）是一道经典的系统设计面试题。它考察你处理海量并发、平衡读写重负载以及在延迟和一致性之间做出权衡的能力。

Part 1: Theory / 理论基础 (5 min)

At its core, a news feed system has two main flows:

1. Feed Publishing (Fan-out): When a user publishes a post, it must be pushed to all their followers' feeds.

2. Feed Retrieval: When a user opens the app, they retrieve their pre-computed or on-the-fly generated feed.

Fan-out on Write (Push Model): Pre-compute the feed during the write phase. Fast reads, but slow writes for users with millions of followers (Justin Bieber problem).

Fan-out on Read (Pull Model): Generate the feed when the user requests it. Fast writes, but slow reads.

Hybrid Model: Push for normal users, pull for celebrities.

核心理论包括两个主要流程：

1. 发布（Fan-out）： 用户发布动态时，推送到所有粉丝的信息流中。

2. 读取： 用户打开应用时，获取预先计算好或实时生成的信息流。

写时扩散（推模式）： 在写入时预先计算信息流。读取快，但对于拥有数百万粉丝的用户（如明星）写入极慢。

读时扩散（拉模式）： 在用户请求时生成信息流。写入快，但读取慢。

混合模式： 普通用户使用推模式，明星使用拉模式。

Part 2: Step-by-Step Implementation / 一步一步实现 (8 min)


[Client] --> [Load Balancer] --> [Web Servers]
                                      |
                 +--------------------+--------------------+
                 |                                         |
        [Post Service]                              [Feed Service]
                 |                                         |
        [Fan-out Workers]                           [Feed Cache (Redis)]
                 |                                         |
    +------------+------------+                            |
    |                         |                            |
[Post DB]               [Graph DB]                 [User Feed DB]
(Cassandra)             (Followers)                (Cassandra/Redis)

Flow Trace:

1. User A posts a message -> Post Service.

2. Post Service saves to Post DB, sends event to Fan-out Workers.

3. Fan-out Workers fetch User A's followers from Graph DB.

4. Workers push the post ID to each follower's Feed Cache.

5. User B (a follower) requests feed -> Feed Service.

6. Feed Service reads User B's Feed Cache (list of post IDs), fetches post details from Post DB, and returns to Client.

代码模拟 (Python-like Pseudocode):


class NewsFeedSystem:
    def __init__(self):
        self.post_db = {}       # post_id -> post_data
        self.feed_cache = {}    # user_id -> list of post_ids
        self.followers_db = {}  # user_id -> list of follower_ids
        
    def publish_post(self, user_id, post_id, content):
        # 1. Save post
        self.post_db[post_id] = {"author": user_id, "content": content}
        
        # 2. Fan-out (Push model)
        followers = self.followers_db.get(user_id, [])
        for follower in followers:
            if follower not in self.feed_cache:
                self.feed_cache[follower] = []
            # Prepend to feed cache
            self.feed_cache[follower].insert(0, post_id)
            
    def get_feed(self, user_id):
        # 1. Fetch post IDs from cache
        post_ids = self.feed_cache.get(user_id, [])
        
        # 2. Hydrate posts
        feed = []
        for pid in post_ids:
            feed.append(self.post_db[pid])
        return feed

Part 3: Edge Cases & Gotchas / 边界情况 (2 min)

- The Celebrity Problem (Hotkey issue): A celebrity with 100M followers posting a tweet will crash the fan-out workers. Use a hybrid approach: don't push celebrity posts; instead, when a user loads their feed, pull the celebrity's recent posts and merge them.

- Cache Eviction: Only keep the top ~1000 posts in the Redis feed cache. Older posts can be fetched from the database if the user scrolls that far.

- 明星问题（热点问题）： 拥有上亿粉丝的明星发帖会压垮 Fan-out 工作节点。解决方案是混合模式：不主动推送明星的帖子，而是在用户刷信息流时，拉取明星的最新帖子并进行合并。

- 缓存淘汰： Redis 中只保留最近的 1000 条动态。如果用户继续向下滚动，再从数据库中读取。

Part 4: Real-World Application / 实际应用 (2 min)

- Twitter / X: Uses a massive Redis cluster for timeline caching. They heavily optimize the fan-out process for different tiers of users.

- Instagram / Facebook: Uses similar hybrid models but with complex machine learning ranking algorithms on top of the chronological feed.

- Twitter / X： 使用庞大的 Redis 集群进行时间线缓存，并针对不同层级的用户深度优化 fan-out 流程。

- Instagram / Facebook： 使用类似的混合模式，但在时间线基础上增加了复杂的机器学习排序算法。

Part 5: Interview Simulation / 面试模拟 (3 min)

1. Q: How do you handle media (images/videos) in posts?

A: Store media in object storage (S3) and use a CDN. The Post DB only stores URLs to the media.

2. Q: What database is best for storing the feed?

A: Cassandra or DynamoDB (NoSQL) is excellent for heavy write workloads and time-series data.

3. Q: How do you implement feed ranking (non-chronological)?

A: The feed service passes the fetched posts to a Ranking Service (ML model) before returning them to the user.

4. Q: What happens if a fan-out worker fails?

A: Use a message queue (Kafka/RabbitMQ) for fan-out tasks. If a worker dies, another worker picks up the unacknowledged message.

5. Q: How to reduce memory usage in the feed cache?

A: Store only [post_id, user_id] in the cache, not the full post content. Hydrate the content during the read phase.

item.description:
🏗️ System Design

🏗️ 系统设计 / System Design — Day 22

设计自动补全 / Typeahead — Design an Autocomplete / Typeahead System

🌍 真实场景 / Real-World Scenario

想象你在谷歌搜索框里输入 "how to"，瞬间出现 10 条建议。这背后是什么？

Imagine typing "how to" in Google's search box and instantly seeing 10 suggestions. What's behind it?

每次用户输入一个字符，系统必须在 <100ms 内返回最相关的补全结果。谷歌、YouTube、Amazon、GitHub 都有这个功能——它看似简单，工程上却很复杂。

Each keystroke must return the most relevant completions in <100ms. Google, YouTube, Amazon, GitHub all have this — it looks simple but is engineering-hard.

🏛️ 架构图 / Architecture


用户输入 "app"
     │
     ▼
[Client] ──(debounce 50ms)──► [API Gateway]
                                    │
                         ┌──────────┴──────────┐
                         ▼                     ▼
                  [Cache Layer]         [Search Service]
                  (Redis, TTL:5min)      │
                                    ┌───┴────────────┐
                                    ▼                ▼
                              [Trie Store]    [ML Ranking]
                              (Prefix Index)  (popularity,
                                              personalization)
                                    │
                                    ▼
                             [Data Pipeline]
                             (Kafka → Spark)
                             counts queries
                             every 10 mins

数据流 / Data Flow:

1. 用户输入 → 客户端 debounce 50ms（减少请求量）

2. API Gateway → 先查 Redis cache

3. Cache miss → Trie 查找 Top-K 前缀

4. ML 模型 rerank（考虑个性化、地理位置）

5. 日志写入 Kafka → Spark 定期更新 Trie 权重

⚙️ 核心数据结构 / Core Data Structure: Trie


             root
           /  |  \
          a   b   c
         /|    \
        p  r    e
       /    \
      p      o
     /|       \
    l  [end]   w
   /            \
  e               s
  [end,"apple,5"]  [end,"browse,3"]

每个节点存储：

- children: dict

- is_end: bool

- top_k: list[{word, freq}] ← 预计算 Top-10，避免遍历

Each node stores precomputed Top-10 completions → avoids traversal on query.

关键优化： 每个节点缓存 Top-K，查询 O(prefix_length)，无需 DFS。

Key optimization: cache Top-K at each node, query is O(prefix_length), no DFS needed.

⚖️ 核心权衡 / Key Tradeoffs

| 决策 | 选项 A | 选项 B | 选择 |

|------|--------|--------|------|

| 存储结构 | Trie (prefix-native) | Inverted index (Elastic) | Trie for latency, ES for fuzzy |

| 更新频率 | 实时 (每次搜索) | 批量 (每10分钟) | 批量—实时代价太高 |

| 个性化 | 全局热榜 | 用户历史 | 两者结合 |

| 多语言 | Unicode Trie | 语言分片 | 按语言分片 |

为什么不实时更新 Trie？

每次搜索都更新 Trie 需要全局锁，QPS 百万级时会变成瓶颈。批量更新（每10分钟）是工程实际选择。

Why not real-time Trie updates? Global locks at million QPS become a bottleneck. Batch updates every 10 min is the engineering reality.

🚫 别踩这个坑 / Common Mistakes

❌ 坑1: 忘记 debounce

每次 keypress 都发请求 → 用户输入 "apple" = 5 个请求。加 debounce 50~100ms，节省 80% 请求。

Not debouncing = 5 requests for "apple". Add debounce 50-100ms, saves 80% of requests.

❌ 坑2: Trie 存完整路径

只存 top-K 在每个节点，不要在查询时做完整 DFS。

Store top-K at each node, don't do full DFS at query time.

❌ 坑3: 忘记限速

恶意用户可以爆破搜索建议接口。Rate limit + IP 封锁必须有。

Malicious users can hammer the suggest endpoint. Rate limiting is non-negotiable.

❌ 坑4: 大写/Unicode 不一致

输入 "Apple" vs "apple" 应该返回一样结果。存储前统一 lowercase + normalize。

"Apple" and "apple" should return same results. Normalize to lowercase before storing.

📐 规模估算 / Scale Numbers

- DAU: 10M 用户

#150 Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation (Medium) — Stack Pattern

🧩 Stack 模式 (3/7) — 基于 Day 21 (Valid Parentheses) 和 Day 24 (Min Stack) 的模版

上次 Min Stack 用栈存最小值，这次用栈做运算——同样的工具，不同的用途。

Last time (Min Stack) we used the stack to track minimums; this time we use it to evaluate — same tool, different job.

🔗 Links

- 🔗 [LeetCode #150](https://leetcode.com/problems/evaluate-reverse-polish-notation/) 🟡 Medium

- 📹 [NeetCode Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iu0082c4HDE)

🌍 现实类比 / Real-World Analogy

逆波兰表达式（RPN）是计算器的内部语言。当你在科学计算器上按 3 4 + 2 *，计算器内部其实就是在用栈处理 RPN。Forth 语言、PostScript 都基于 RPN。

RPN is the internal language of calculators. When you press 3 4 + 2 on a scientific calculator, it's processing RPN with a stack internally. Forth, PostScript are all RPN-based.*

🧩 问题 / Problem

给你一个字符串数组，表示逆波兰表达式：

Given a string array representing a Reverse Polish Notation expression:


Input: ["2","1","+","3","*"]
Output: 9
Explanation: ((2 + 1) * 3) = 9

Input: ["4","13","5","/","+"]
Output: 6
Explanation: (4 + (13 / 5)) = 6

规则 / Rules: 遇到数字 → 入栈；遇到运算符 → 弹出两个数计算 → 结果入栈。

Rule: number → push; operator → pop two, compute, push result.

🗺️ 映射到模版 / Map to Template

通用栈模版： 遍历 → 条件判断 → push 或 pop

这道题的变化： 不是找"下一个更大元素"，而是把数字当操作数，遇到运算符就出栈计算


stack = []
for token in tokens:
    if token is NUMBER:
        stack.append(int(token))     # push
    else:
        b = stack.pop()              # 注意顺序！b是后弹出的
        a = stack.pop()              # a是先弹出的（先入栈的）
        result = apply(a, op, b)
        stack.append(result)         # push result back
return stack[0]

关键陷阱 / Key Trap: 弹出顺序！a - b 中，a 是先入栈的（先到达），所以：

先 pop b（后到），再 pop a（先到），计算 a op b。

Pop order matters! For a - b: a was pushed first, so pop b first, then a.

🐍 Python 解法 / Solution


def evalRPN(tokens: list[str]) -> int:
    stack = []
    ops = {
        '+': lambda a, b: a + b,
        '-': lambda a, b: a - b,
        '*': lambda a, b: a * b,
        '/': lambda a, b: int(a / b)  # truncate toward zero (not //!)
    }
    
    for token in tokens:
        if token in ops:
            b = stack.pop()   # second operand (pushed last)
            a = stack.pop()   # first operand (pushed first)
            stack.append(ops[token](a, b))
        else:
            stack.append(int(token))
    
    return stack[0]

# Trace: ["2","1","+","3","*"]
# "2" → stack: [2]
# "1" → stack: [2, 1]
# "+" → pop 1,2 → 2+1=3 → stack: [3]
# "3" → stack: [3, 3]
# "*" → pop 3,3 → 3*3=9 → stack: [9]
# return 9 ✓

注意 / 的处理！

Python // 向负无穷截断：-7 // 2 = -4

题目要求向零截断：-7 / 2 = -3

所以用 int(a / b)，不用 a // b！

Python // truncates toward negative infinity, but the problem wants truncation toward zero. Use int(a/b) not a//b!

📊 复杂度 / Complexity

- 时间 Time: O(n) — 每个 token 处理一次

- 空间 Space: O(n) — 栈最大存 n/2 个数字

成长型思维 / Growth Mindset

题目：告诉我你收到了一次很难听的反馈。你是怎么应对的？

*Tell me about a time you received tough feedback. How did you respond?*

🎯 为什么这道题很重要 / Why This Matters

这道题考察的不是你有没有犯过错，而是你如何面对批评。

Senior/Staff 工程师的标志之一：能从批评中学习，而不是防御或逃避。

面试官在看：自我认知、情绪成熟度、持续改进的能力。

This question doesn't test whether you made mistakes — it tests how you handle criticism. A marker of Senior/Staff engineers: learning from feedback instead of defending or deflecting. Interviewers look for: self-awareness, emotional maturity, capacity to grow.

⭐ STAR 框架 / STAR Breakdown

S — Situation（背景）:

设置具体场景。是代码评审？设计评审？绩效评估？

避免模糊的 "有一次我的老板批评了我"。

Set a specific context. Code review? Design review? Performance review? Avoid vague "my manager criticized me once."

T — Task（任务）:

你当时做的是什么项目/决策？

What were you working on or what decision had you made?

A — Action（行动）:

这是关键！要展示：

1. 你冷静地接受了反馈（没有立刻防御）

2. 你主动寻求理解（问了澄清问题）

3. 你具体做出了改变

This is the key! Show: 1) You received feedback calmly (no immediate defensiveness), 2) You sought to understand (asked clarifying questions), 3) You made concrete changes.

R — Result（结果）:

量化结果 + 长期影响（你从中学到了什么习惯？）

Quantify the result + long-term impact (what habit did you develop?)

❌ 差答案 vs ✅ 好答案 / Bad vs Good

❌ 差答案:

> "有一次我老板说我沟通不好，我就多发了些邮件，后来他满意了。"

问题：太模糊、没有自我反思、没有展示成长。

Too vague, no self-reflection, no demonstrated growth.

✅ 好答案 (Sample):

> "在做一个后端服务重构时，我的 Tech Lead 在代码评审中说我的 PR 很难 review——改动超过 2000 行，没有原子化。我当时第一反应是有点委屈，因为我觉得改动是连贯的。

>

> 但我没有立刻反驳，而是先问他：'你觉得最难理解的是哪部分？' 他指出我把接口变更和实现变更混在一起了。

>

> 我重新把 PR 拆成 4 个：接口定义 → 数据层 → 业务逻辑 → 集成测试。每个 PR 独立可测试。

>

> 结果 review 时间从 3 天缩短到 1 天，后来团队把'PR ≤ 400 行'写进了我们的开发规范。这个习惯我现在每个项目都在用。"

为什么好： 具体场景、初始情绪诚实、主动提问理解根因、行动可量化、有长期影响。

Why it works: specific scenario, honest about initial emotion, proactively sought root cause, quantifiable action, lasting impact.

💎 Senior/Staff 加分项 / Senior/Staff Tips

展示元认知 (metacognition):

> "那次反馈让我意识到，我倾向于在「把东西做完」和「让别人容易理解」之间优先前者。这是一个我持续在调整的倾向。"

展示你帮助他人成长:

> "后来我成为了团队的 code review mentorship 负责人，把这个经验传给了新人。"

避免假谦虚:

不要说 "我最大的缺点是工作太努力了"——面试官会翻白眼。

Don't say "my biggest weakness is working too hard" — interviewers will roll their eyes.

🗝️ 关键要点 / Key Takeaways

1. 诚实 > 完美 — 展示真实的成长比假装从不犯错更有说服力

2. 行动比情绪重要 — 你感受到委屈是正常的，关键是你做了什么

3. 量化长期影响 — 把个人成长转化为团队/系统改进

4. 成长型思维的核心： 失败是数据，不是定义

1. Honest > Perfect — real growth > pretending perfection. 2. Action > Emotion — feeling stung is normal, what matters is what you did. 3. Quantify long-term impact. 4. Growth mindset core: failure is data, not identity.
